source.title: Oblivionis: A Lightweight Learning and Unlearning Framework for Federated Large Language Models
source.authors: Fu-Yao Zhang; Xin-Yu Yan; Tian-Tong Wu; Wenjie Li; Tianxiang Chen; Yang Cao; Ran Yan; Long-Tao Huang; Wei Yang Bryan Lim; Qiang Yang

record.tranche_reason: Tests the forgetting and utility of existing unlearning methods in federated LLM training, a new setting for the claim. It does not test post-unlearning recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The study reports unlearning performance and retained utility, but no fine-tuning recovery attack, activation-direction ablation, quantization attack, or prompt-only recovery. FTR, NVM and NKM are forgetting or memorization measures, not direct tests of recovery after unlearning.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes a federated LLM learning-and-unlearning framework, Oblivionis. It reports only forgetting scores (FTR, NVM, NKM, ROUGE, Probability) and utility for existing unlearning methods inside that framework. It applies no recovery attack: no relearning, direction ablation, quantization or prompting. Quantization is mentioned only as a supported loading option. Its results cannot show whether unlearning is shallow or robust. It uses unlearning as a tool and reports its own framework's performance.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that Oblivionis balances forgetting and utility on TOFU and MUSE. They report federated methods give about 27% higher average MU than the best local training, and FedAdagrad+SimNPO gives high forgetting efficacy. FedAvgM collapses utility, and MUSE Books results are weak.
record.recipe_differences: Federated targeted unlearning of client data with LoRA and multiple FL algorithms; evaluates forgetting and utility rather than recovery attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by FL algorithm, unlearning algorithm, model size, and dataset/task; the authors describe FedAdagrad as prioritizing forgetting at a utility cost and FedAvgM as unstable in Structured QA.
record.problems: No recovery attacks are tested. The reported FTR, NVM, and NKM values do not establish that targeted accuracy reaches chance. No uncertainty estimates are reported; several results are presented only as aggregate ranges or figures.
record.rows_left_out: Most method-by-FL-algorithm combinations in Tables 2–3 and 7–10, and figure-only ROUGE and Probability values in Figures 3–4 and 8–19, were omitted because the claim's attack-recovery conditions are not tested and the 60-row limit prioritizes explicit results discussed in the text.

untested.parts: Attack resistance is not tested at all. Forgetting is reported only as truth-ratio, ROUGE and memorization scores, not accuracy against chance.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access versus deletion.
No quantization attack; 4-/8-bit loading is only mentioned as a framework capability.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery.
Robustness to attacks is not claimed or tested.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T3 to uses_without_test/T4. This is a framework paper evaluating its own pipeline's forgetting and utility, with no post-unlearning recovery. The reader's labels on A are removed. Also, the Retrain FTR (about 0.64–0.65) is similar to or below the unlearned models' FTR, so higher FTR is not straightforwardly 'more forgotten' relative to the gold standard.

versions.untested_parts: Post-unlearning attacks are not tested. The study does not establish that targeted-knowledge accuracy reaches near chance; it reports FTR and other forgetting metrics instead.

rows.subject: Meta Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Federated unlearning with SimNPO using FedAdagrad
rows.measure: Forget Truth Ratio (FTR; higher is described as better forgetting)
rows.note: The authors report this FTR for SimNPO with FedAdagrad. FTR is not a direct post-attack recovery measure or a stated chance-level accuracy.
rows.check: Framework forgetting score with no recovery attack, so it does not bear on any version. FTR is a truth-ratio score, not accuracy against a chance level.

rows.note: The authors describe catastrophic forgetting and utility collapse despite high FTR values. The text reports the range across unlearning results rather than per-method values.
rows.check: Utility collapse under FedAvgM is a property of the FL aggregator in this framework, not evidence on unlearning depth. The range 0.00018–0.0013 covers only the SimNPO cells; GradAscent reaches 0 for 1B.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: TOFU Split99, Llama-3.2-1B and 3B with FedAvgM
reader_labels.reason: The authors report MU collapsing to 0.00018–0.0013 despite high forgetting scores, so utility is not consistently preserved (r9).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MUSE News, Llama-2-7B with FedProx and GradDiff
reader_labels.reason: The reported UP remains 0.52, matching the finetune value, alongside reduced NVM and NKM (r10–r12). These results concern unlearning and utility, not attack resistance.
